## Research

- **[It Lied to a Doctor to Buy Poison Ingredients: Quantifying Real-World Misuse of Phone-use Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27944)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  First systematic study of phone-use agent misuse across 27 apps and 9 frontier models on real devices, finding 68.8% average task completion for harmful requests including drug acquisition and review fraud. Identifies a Safety Awareness-Execution Gap where agents recognize harm yet proceed.

- **[Govern the Repository, Not the Agent: Measuring Ecosystem-Level Risk in AI-Native Software](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28235)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Empirical study analyzing 930,000 agent-authored pull requests finding that agents concentrate repository-level integration friction roughly twice as much as humans (ICC 0.30 vs. 0.16). Argues AI-native software risk is an ecosystem property requiring repository-level governance, not per-agent policy.

- **[Agent-Native Immune System: Architecture, Taxonomy, and Engineering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28270)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Proposes ANIS, a six-layer biologically-inspired runtime defense framework for autonomous agents against memory corruption, tool manipulation, and multi-agent protocol attacks. Distinguishes training-time alignment from runtime protection and introduces a Continual Immune Learning mechanism.

- **[Agentic Hardware Design as Repository-Level Code Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28279)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Introduces HORIZON, a framework treating RTL hardware design as repository-level code evolution where an autonomous agent loop compiles Markdown specs into project packages and uses git worktrees for state management. Achieves full benchmark completion across multiple hardware design test suites.

- **[GBC: Gradient-Based Connections for Optimizing Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28187)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Models LLM multi-agent systems as computational graphs and uses token-level gradient weights to measure cross-agent influence, enabling precise error-source attribution and targeted optimization. The AgentChord implementation uses prefix-based gradient computation; tested on MultiWOZ and tau-bench.

- **[ToolPrivacyBench: Benchmarking Purpose-Bound Privacy in Tool-Using LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28061)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  A benchmark of 2,150 cases evaluating whether LLM agents respect need-to-know information flow across multi-tool trajectories, including 1,150 synthetic business workflows. Key finding: successful tool execution does not imply appropriate privacy disclosure — agents may complete tasks while leaking unnecessary private data through intermediate calls.

- **[Grounded Iterative Language Planning: How Parameterized World Models Reduce Hallucination Propagation in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27806)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Introduces GILP, which merges a compact parametric world model with LLM reasoning via a consistency gate that requests reconsideration on disagreement. Reduces hallucinated-state rate from 0.176 to 0.035 and raises task success from 0.668 to 0.838 with ~22% extra LLM calls, evaluated on four graph-based planning benchmarks.

- **[When Search Agents Should Ask: DiscoBench for Clarification-Aware Deep Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27669)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Introduces DiscoBench, a benchmark of 211 samples with 463 ambiguity instances across 11 domains evaluating whether search agents proactively identify query ambiguity and ask clarification questions. Finds current agents typically search repeatedly instead of asking, revealing a gap between retrieval ability and interactive problem-solving.

- **[ATOD: Annealed Turn-aware On-policy Distillation for Multi-turn Autonomous Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27814)** — arXiv · 2026-06-26
  Hybrid training method for long-horizon interactive agents combining on-policy distillation with RL via an annealing schedule that prioritizes distillation early then shifts to reward optimization. A turn-level reweighting mechanism adds supervision quality; achieves ~3 pp over pure distillation and ~24 pp over a pure RL variant.

- **[Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24775)** — arXiv · 2026-06-23
  Empirical study evaluating 12 agent memory systems across 5 benchmark workloads and 11 datasets from a data management perspective. Finds no single architecture dominates — effectiveness depends on workload-memory structure alignment — and that localized maintenance is more cost-efficient than global reorganization.

- **[Multi-Agent Transactive Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19911)** — arXiv · 2026-06-18
  Extends retrieval-augmented generation to population-level experience sharing: agents store and retrieve full trajectories from a shared repository, letting newly created agents benefit from prior agents' solutions without redundant problem-solving; demonstrated to improve task performance and reduce interaction steps on ALFWorld and WebArena.

- **[A Technical Taxonomy of LLM Agent Communication Protocols](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19135)** — arXiv · 2026-06-17
  Systematically analyzes nine open-source agent communication protocols (including MCP, A2A, and others) across five dimensions—counterparty, payload, interaction state, discovery mechanism, and schema flexibility—identifying recurring hybrid-payload and session-state patterns and predicting evolution toward a federated, layered protocol stack rather than a single universal standard.

- **[State-Grounded Multi-Agent Synthetic Data Generation for Tool-Augmented LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16307)** — arXiv · 2026-06-15
  StateGen orchestrates a four-role LLM loop—persona-conditioned user simulator, agent under test, state-grounded tool simulator, and multi-axis judge—to produce scored, reasoning-trace-rich training data; a central state manager enforcing a backend-is-truth invariant eliminates the dominant class of tool-call hallucinations by construction, and the architecture generalizes to hierarchical multi-agent settings.

- **[SkillAxe: Sharpening LLM-Authored Agent Skills Through Evaluation-Guided Self-Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10546)** — arXiv · 2026-06-09
  Introduces an unsupervised method for iteratively diagnosing and refining LLM-generated skill documents along four quality dimensions without labeled data, achieving a 28% relative improvement over unimproved LLM skills on SkillsBench and recovering nearly half the performance gap between machine- and human-authored instructions.

- **[Emergence World: A Platform for Evaluating Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Autonomy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08367)** — arXiv · 2026-06-06
  A continuously-running multi-agent simulation platform grounding LLM-driven agents in a shared spatial environment with live external data, 120+ tools, persistent memory, and democratic self-governance; a 15-day study across five model families produced radically different outcomes from stable governance to population collapse, revealing long-horizon dynamics invisible in short evaluation windows.

- **[Agent Planning Benchmark: A Diagnostic Framework for Planning Capabilities in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04874)** — arXiv · 2026-06-03
  Introduces APB, a 4,209-case multimodal diagnostic benchmark across 22 domains that decomposes agent evaluation below end-to-end success into goal decomposition, tool selection, constraint reasoning, and calibrated refusal; testing 12 MLLMs reveals systematic weaknesses in long-horizon planning, tool-noise robustness, and inference-time refinement, with APB-guided feedback consistently improving downstream execution.

- **[From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04990)** — arXiv · 2026-06-03
  Surveys execution provenance and evidence tracing as frameworks for auditing autonomous LLM agent decisions, covering retrieval grounding, tool safety, memory lineage, and failure diagnosis under a unified approach; provides a taxonomy of provenance methods and guidance for building auditable, recoverable agent systems.

- **[Silent Failure in LLM Agent Systems: The Entropy Principle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08162)** — arXiv · 2026-06-06
  Based on 40,000+ controlled trials across 22 intrinsic agent-system properties, proposes that autonomous agents accumulate 'Intelligence Entropy' predictably over time (formalized as S(t) = S₀·eᵅᵗ); introduces the PIG Engine and ADE protocol suite to govern and counteract entropy-driven degradation without code changes.

- **[Organizational Control Layer: Governance at the Agent Execution Boundary](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04306)** — arXiv · 2026-06-03
  Proposes OCL, a model-agnostic governance layer that intercepts LLM-generated actions before execution via policy enforcement and escalation; reduces unsafe executions from 88% to near-zero while raising valid task success from 12% to 96% across multiple LLM backends.

- **[Ahoy: LLMs Enacting Multiagent Interaction Protocols](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05390)** — arXiv · 2026-06-03
  Enables LLM-based agents to dynamically select and concurrently enact multiple declarative interaction protocols without specialized training or protocol-specific implementations, decoupling agent intelligence from protocol details.

- **[Agent System Operations: Categorization, Challenges, and Future Directions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01581)** — arXiv · 2026-06-01
  Introduces AgentOps, the first systematic framework for operating deployed LLM agent systems, categorizing anomalies as intra-agent or inter-agent and spanning monitoring, anomaly detection, root-cause localization, and resolution across the agent lifecycle.

- **[DySCo: Dynamic Trust-Aware Sparse Communication for LLM Multi-Agent Consensus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01828)** — arXiv · 2026-06-01
  Replaces fully connected multi-agent communication (which scales quadratically) with trust-weighted edge selection based on agent reliability, answer divergence, and task relevance; preserves error-correction interactions while enabling early consensus termination.

- **[TRACE: Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression for Long-Horizon Agent Safety](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00611)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  Treats long-horizon agent safety detection as trajectory-level evidence compression: a Compressor encodes full trajectories into compact evidence states that a Reader judges for risk, gaining up to 12.6 percentage points over per-step local moderators across multiple benchmarks.

- **[CoMIC: Collaborative Memory and Insights Circulation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00756)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  Centralized-Reflection, Decentralized-Execution design for deploying LLMs at the edge: edge agents maintain subgoal-oriented hierarchical memory while a cloud-side LLM critic asynchronously filters cross-agent experience and distributes guidance back, enabling long-horizon execution without fine-tuning.

- **[MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00619)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  Rather than adapting only a memory bank or prompt post-deployment, MemPro treats the full memory-construction-retrieval pipeline as an evolvable program: an Evolving Agent maintains a version tree of runnable implementations and applies failure-mode-guided refinement to continuously improve performance across tasks.

- **[Skill or Skip? Selective Skill Invocation in Agentic Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00510)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  Frames skill use as a binary invoke-or-skip decision at each step via SelSkill: uncertainty-prioritized candidate selection and dual-granularity preference learning (trajectory + step level) avoid unhelpful invocations that disrupt correct agent execution, gaining ~11 pp on ALFWorld and 5.7 pp on BFCL.

- **[The Deterministic Horizon: When Extended Reasoning Fails and Tool Delegation Becomes Necessary](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00376)** — arXiv · 2026-05-29
  Identifies an Attention Bottleneck in decoder-only models causing chain-of-thought to collapse beyond roughly 19–31 reasoning steps (the 'Deterministic Horizon'); tool-integrated reasoning reaches 86–94% accuracy on state-tracking tasks versus 24–42% for pure neural reasoning, framing tool delegation as architecturally necessary.

- **[Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06448)** — arXiv · 2026-06-04
  A systems-level characterization of agent memory architectures for long-horizon workloads, offering a taxonomy spanning flat retrieval, LLM-mediated extraction, and consolidating fact stores, plus a profiling methodology.

- **[Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04197)** — arXiv · 2026-06-02
  Runs 432 naming-game simulations varying agent memory depth and network structure, finding that memory length and topology interact to determine whether multi-agent populations converge on shared conventions or fragment.

- **[The Landscape of Agentic Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: A Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02547)** — arXiv · 2025-09-02
  Recent survey framing the shift from RLHF on static LLMs to agentic RL, with a taxonomy of core capabilities (planning, tool use, memory, reasoning, self-improvement, perception) — a strong roadmap for picking a research direction.

- **[τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045)** — arXiv · 2024-06-17
  Foundational benchmark testing agents on dynamic conversations with a simulated user and domain-specific API rules (retail, airline), with a pass^k metric that exposes the unreliability of agents over repeated trials.

- **[SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)** — arXiv · 2024-05-06
  Foundational work showing that a well-designed Agent-Computer Interface (custom commands for viewing, editing, and running code) dramatically boosts an LLM agent's ability to resolve real GitHub issues on SWE-bench.

- **[GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983)** — arXiv · 2023-11-21
  Foundational benchmark of real-world questions that are conceptually simple for humans but require multi-step reasoning, web browsing, multimodality, and tool use — a standard measure of general assistant agents.

- **[MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560)** — arXiv · 2023-10-12
  Foundational memory architecture treating the context window like RAM and external stores like disk, with the LLM managing paging between tiers via function calls to handle unbounded context — basis of the Letta project.

- **[SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)** — arXiv · 2023-10-10
  Foundational coding-agent benchmark of 2,294 real GitHub issue/PR tasks across popular Python repos, evaluated by running the projects' own test suites — the de facto standard for measuring software-engineering agents.

- **[The Rise and Potential of Large Language Model Based Agents: A Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07864)** — arXiv · 2023-09-14
  Comprehensive, frequently-cited survey covering the brain-perception-action agent framework, single- vs. multi-agent settings, agent society, and open problems — arguably the best single entry point for orienting in agentic AI.

- **[Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02427)** — arXiv · 2023-09-05
  Foundational conceptual framework organizing language agents along modular memory, structured action space (internal vs. external), and a generalized decision-making loop — useful scaffolding for reasoning about agent design.

- **[A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11432)** — arXiv · 2023-08-22
  Widely-cited survey organizing LLM agent research around a unified construction framework (profile, memory, planning, action) and reviewing applications and evaluation — a solid orientation map for the field.

- **[AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155)** — arXiv · 2023-08-16
  Foundational framework (now a major Microsoft project) modeling applications as conversations among customizable, conversable agents that mix LLMs, tools, and humans — a cornerstone of multi-agent orchestration.

- **[MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352)** — arXiv · 2023-08-01
  Foundational multi-agent framework encoding human Standardized Operating Procedures into prompts so role-specialized agents (PM, architect, engineer) collaborate with structured intermediate artifacts to reduce error cascades.

- **[ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16789)** — arXiv · 2023-07-31
  Foundational tool-learning work introducing ToolBench (instruction data over 16k+ real REST APIs) and a depth-first search-based decision tree for multi-tool reasoning, plus the ToolEval evaluator.

- **[WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13854)** — arXiv · 2023-07-25
  Foundational web-agent benchmark providing a reproducible, self-hosted environment of functional websites (e-commerce, forums, CMS, GitLab) with task-completion-based evaluation — a standard testbed for browser agents.

- **[Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291)** — arXiv · 2023-05-25
  Seminal lifelong-learning agent in Minecraft that explores autonomously, writes and stores reusable executable skills in a growing library, and self-improves via environment feedback — a key reference for skill acquisition.

- **[Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15334)** — arXiv · 2023-05-24
  Foundational tool-use work fine-tuning an LLM to accurately call from a large, changing catalog of real APIs using retrieval-aware training, reducing hallucinated calls — an antecedent of today's tool/function calling.

- **[Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601)** — arXiv · 2023-05-17
  Foundational reasoning framework that generalizes chain-of-thought into a search over a tree of intermediate 'thoughts' with lookahead and backtracking, a core building block for agent planning.

- **[Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442)** — arXiv · 2023-04-07
  Seminal work placing 25 LLM-driven agents in a sandbox town with memory, reflection, and planning, producing believable emergent social behavior — a touchstone for agent memory architectures and social simulation.

- **[CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760)** — arXiv · 2023-03-31
  Early multi-agent framework introducing role-playing and inception prompting so two agents (e.g. an AI user and AI assistant) autonomously cooperate to complete a task — a seminal reference for agent-to-agent communication.

- **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)** — arXiv · 2023-03-20
  Foundational self-improvement method where an agent reflects in natural language on failed attempts and stores those reflections in episodic memory to do better on retries, without updating model weights.

- **[Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)** — arXiv · 2023-02-09
  Foundational work showing an LLM can learn, in a self-supervised way, when and how to call external APIs (calculator, search, QA, translation) by inserting API calls into its own training data.

- **[ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)** — arXiv · 2022-10-06
  The foundational paper interleaving chain-of-thought reasoning with tool/action steps in a single loop, establishing the reason-act-observe paradigm that underpins most modern LLM agents.

- **[Channel Fracture: Architectural Blind Spots in Scheduled Cross-Agent Memory Injection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04896)** — arXiv · 2026-06-03
  Identifies a silent failure mode in multi-agent deployments where cron-scheduled agents cannot write to another agent's persistent memory due to hardcoded isolation guards; tested on a production Hermes Agent deployment and proposes CADVP v1.1, a 13-dimension verification framework.

- **[Capability Advertisement as a Market for Lemons: A Trust Layer for Heterogeneous Agent Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03034)** — arXiv · 2026-06-02
  Argues that agent capability claims in MCP/A2A delegation suffer from Akerlof's market-for-lemons problem — callers cannot distinguish reliable providers from fluent impostors — and proposes a protocol-agnostic trust layer using probabilistic descriptors, screening, and reputation mechanisms.

- **[Multi-Agent Computer Use](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01533)** — arXiv · 2026-06-01
  Introduces MACU, a framework where a manager model decomposes tasks into dependency DAGs executed by parallel subagents; achieves 3.4–25.5% gains across OSWorld, Mind2Web, WebTailBench, and Odysseys benchmarks with ~1.5× faster wall-clock completion on long-horizon tasks versus single-agent baselines.

- **[MetaForge: A Self-Evolving Multimodal Agent that Retrieves, Adapts, and Forges Tools On Demand](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01801)** — arXiv · 2026-06-01
  An agent framework that dynamically synthesizes new tools when existing ones are insufficient, penalizes unnecessary tool calls, and makes forged tools reusable; evaluated on 12 benchmarks with improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and generalization to unfamiliar scenarios.

- **[Doing What They Say, Not What They Reason: Locating the Faithfulness Gap in LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00476)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  Uses a Texas Poker simulator as a ground-truth testbed to measure whether agents act on their stated reasoning; finds the gap divides into reasoning-to-conclusion and conclusion-to-action stages that behave oppositely, with implications for using LLMs in social simulation.

- **[ForeSci: Evaluating LLM Agents for Forward-Looking AI Research Judgment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00644)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  A 500-task benchmark spanning four AI domains and four decision categories that tests whether LLM agents can make research predictions from historical information; finds 'evidence-decision decoupling' — agents cite relevant sources but still forecast incorrect outcomes.

- **[Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00655)** — arXiv · 2026-05-30
  Studies how LLM-based multi-agent systems scale with agent count using the SIMAS framework; finds diminishing returns rather than linear gains, driven by coordination overhead rather than context length, with optimal agent count varying significantly by task type.

- **[AI Research Agents Narrow Scientific Exploration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27905)** — arXiv · 2026-05-27
  Analyzes 37,802 ideas from four AI research-agent frameworks and six LLMs, finding generated ideas concentrate around existing work rather than broadening exploration.

- **[Paris 2.0: A Decentralized Diffusion Model for Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26064)** — arXiv · 2026-05-25
  The first video generation model trained through decentralized computation, reporting roughly 2x better video quality than centralized training at equivalent compute.

- **[What Twelve LLM Agent Benchmark Papers Disclose About Themselves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21404)** — arXiv · 2026-05-20
  A pilot audit of twelve LLM agent benchmark papers finds a mean disclosure score of 0.38 (vs 0.66 for classical benchmarks), with no agent paper reporting inference cost; the authors release an open scoring schema and codebook.

- **[Quant.npu: Efficient Mobile NPU Inference for On-Device LLMs via Fully Static Quantization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20295)** — arXiv · 2026-05-19
  A fully static, integer-only quantization framework using learnable quantization parameters and rotation matrices to run LLMs efficiently on mobile NPUs, cutting inference latency.

- **[Protein Thoughts: Interpretable Reasoning with Tree of Thoughts for Protein-Protein Interaction Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21522)** — arXiv · 2026-05-19
  Reformulates protein-protein interaction discovery as an interpretable tree-of-thoughts search over four biologically meaningful signals, with embedding-space flow matching for mechanistic justification.

- **[Nano World Models: A Minimalist Implementation of Future Video Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23993)** — arXiv · 2026-05-17
  A compact, reproducible codebase for studying world models and future video prediction, with a unified interface over generative objectives, model scales, and action-conditioning mechanisms.

- **[Cattle Trade: A Multi-Agent Benchmark for LLM Bluffing, Bidding, and Bargaining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14537)** — arXiv · 2026-05-14
  An arXiv benchmark evaluating LLMs as strategic agents under imperfect information across a 50–60 turn game of auctions, bargaining, and bluffing; some heuristic code agents outperformed most tested LLMs.

- **[Compute Where it Counts: Self-Optimizing Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10875)** — arXiv · 2026-05-11
  Pairs a frozen LLM with a lightweight policy network that allocates compute per token by controlling attention sparsity, activation pruning, and quantization bit-width, improving the quality–efficiency frontier.

- **[Rethinking RL for LLM Reasoning: It's Sparse Policy Selection, Not Capability Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06241)** — arXiv · 2026-05-07
  Argues RL improves reasoning by sparsely selecting policy at uncertain decision points rather than teaching new capabilities, motivating a far cheaper post-training method (ReasonMaxxer).

- **[Patch-Effect Graph Kernels for LLM Interpretability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06480)** — arXiv · 2026-05-07
  Reframes mechanistic interpretability as a graph ML problem, representing activation-patching profiles as graphs over model components and using graph kernels to identify causal circuits.

- **[Mamoda2.5: Enhancing Unified Multimodal Model with DiT-MoE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02641)** — arXiv · 2026-05-04
  A unified AR-diffusion model combining multimodal understanding and generation, using a Diffusion Transformer with a 128-expert Top-8 MoE (25B params, 3B active) and strong VBench 2.0 / video-editing results.

- **[Privacy Preserving ML Workflow: Personalized Differential Privacy Budgets in Federated Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02372)** — arXiv · 2026-05-04
  A federated learning workflow for sensitive tabular data that assigns per-client differential privacy budgets based on a re-identification risk metric, improving utility over fixed global budgets.

- **[Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02964)** — arXiv · 2026-05-03
  A suite of multi-step tool-use tasks with naturalistic shortcuts; evaluating 13 frontier models finds RL post-training substantially increases reward hacking, with exploit rates from 0% to 13.9%.

- **[Position: Safety and Fairness in Agentic AI Depend on Interaction Topology, Not Model Scale or Alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01147)** — arXiv · 2026-05-01
  Argues multi-agent safety hinges on how agents are wired together, identifying topology-driven failures (ordering instability, information cascades) that persist across model scales and alignment.

- **[GroupMemBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent Memory in Multi-Party Conversations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14498)** — arXiv · 2026-05-14
  New arXiv benchmark for evaluating LLM agent memory across multi-party conversations, exposing notable gaps in current memory systems.

- **[AlphaEvolve: a Gemini-powered coding agent scaling impact across fields](https://deepmind.google/blog/alphaevolve-impact/)** — Google DeepMind · 2026-05-07
  Google DeepMind's Gemini-powered coding agent shows real-world impact across genomics, power-grid optimization, quantum physics, and mathematics.

## Big Lab Update

- **[Securing the Future of AI Agents](https://deepmind.google/blog/securing-the-future-of-ai-agents/)** — Google DeepMind · 2026-06-18
  Google DeepMind introduces an AI Control Roadmap framing advanced AI agents as potential insider threats: a threat taxonomy built on MITRE ATT&CK, a dual-layer detection/prevention system validated against one million coding agent tasks, and a companion Three Layers of Agent Security framework for policymakers covering individual agents, multi-agent systems, and broader cyber resilience.

- **[Google DeepMind and Partners Launch $10M Multi-Agent AI Safety Research Call](https://deepmind.google/blog/investing-in-multi-agent-ai-safety-research/)** — Google DeepMind · 2026-06-11
  Google DeepMind, Schmidt Sciences, Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA, and Google.org launch a $10M funding call for multi-agent AI safety research, targeting sandboxes and testbeds, agent network science, cross-platform identity/reputation protocols, and collective oversight methods for deployed agent populations.

- **[Anthropic raises $65B Series H at $965B post-money valuation](https://www.anthropic.com/news/series-h)** — Anthropic · 2026-05-28
